questions.q: In the Standard Model the elementary particles are described as being either fermions or bosons. Which statement correctly describes the fermions?
options: Fermions are the gauge bosons that carry the forces between particles
Fermions are the particles that combine to make up matter; they have half-integer spin and obey Pauli's Exclusion Principle
Fermions are scalar particles, like the Higgs, whose only job is to give other particles mass
Fermions are the photons, gluons and W and Z bosons of the Standard Model
questions.explanation: In the Standard Model, fermions are the matter particles that combine to make up matter, with half-integer spin and obeying Pauli's Exclusion Principle. The force carriers are the bosons; the Higgs is a scalar boson, not a fermion.

questions.q: In the Standard Model, gauge bosons carry the fundamental forces. Which set correctly matches each force to its carrier, including the force the Standard Model does not explain?
options: Photons carry the strong nuclear force; gluons carry the electromagnetic force; W and Z bosons carry gravity

Gluons carry the strong nuclear force; photons carry the electromagnetic force; W and Z bosons carry the weak nuclear force; gravity has no boson, so it is the one force the Standard Model does not explain
The Higgs boson carries the strong force; photons carry gravity; gluons carry the weak force
Gravity is carried by the graviton, which the Standard Model has confirmed alongside the photon and gluon
questions.explanation: Gauge bosons come in three forms: photons (electromagnetic force), gluons that hold quarks together (strong nuclear force), and the W and Z bosons (weak nuclear force). No boson has been found that carries the gravitational force, so gravity is the one force the Standard Model does not explain.

questions.q: Leptons are described as fundamental particles with no internal structure. Which particles are the leptons?
options: The proton, the neutron and the pion
The electron, the muon and the tau, together with their three neutrinos
The up, down, charm, strange, top and bottom quarks
The photon, the gluon and the W and Z bosons
questions.explanation: Leptons are fundamental particles with no internal structure: the electron, muon and tau (each negatively charged) and their neutrinos. The electron is the lepton found in atoms and it determines the chemical properties of elements. Quarks and the force-carrying bosons are not leptons.

questions.q: Hadrons are particles with internal structure, made up of quarks. How do mesons and baryons differ?
options: A meson is a combination of two quarks, whereas a baryon is a combination of three quarks; the proton and neutron are baryons
A meson is three quarks, whereas a baryon is two quarks; the proton is a meson
Mesons and baryons are both leptons with no internal structure
A meson is a single quark, whereas a baryon is a quark plus an antiquark
questions.explanation: Hadrons are made of quarks. Mesons are a combination of two quarks (one quark and one antiquark); baryons are combinations of three quarks. The proton and neutron are baryons. The classic trap is to swap these or to call a proton a meson.

questions.q: A proton is a baryon composed of two up quarks and one down quark (uud). Using the quark charges, show that the proton has a charge of plus one unit.
questions.given: Composition uud; up quark charge \(+\tfrac{2}{3}\), down quark charge \(-\tfrac{1}{3}\) (in units of the elementary charge)
questions.explanation: The fractional quark charges add to a whole number: the two up quarks contribute \(+\tfrac{2}{3}\) each and the down quark \(-\tfrac{1}{3}\), giving \(+1\). Marks are earned by showing the addition explicitly, not just stating 'uud'.

questions.q: A neutron is composed of one up quark and two down quarks (udd). Using the quark charges of \(+\tfrac{2}{3}\) for up and \(-\tfrac{1}{3}\) for down, show that the neutron is neutral.
questions.given: Composition udd; up quark charge \(+\tfrac{2}{3}\), down quark charge \(-\tfrac{1}{3}\)
questions.explanation: One up and two down quarks are required to produce a neutral particle with a charge of 0. Note the proton (uud) and neutron (udd) differ by just a single quark.

questions.q: From memory: according to the Standard Model, all the visible matter in the universe is composed of which particles?
keyPoints: All the visible (ordinary, stable) matter is composed of first-generation quarks and leptons.
That means up quarks and down quarks (bound into protons and neutrons of the nucleus).
Plus electrons, which are leptons, around the outside.
The heavier generations (charm, strange, top, bottom, muon, tau, their neutrinos) are not needed to build ordinary matter.
questions.explanation: If you recalled 'first-generation quarks and leptons — up quarks, down quarks and electrons', grade yourself Good or Easy. If you only listed protons and neutrons without naming the quarks, grade it Hard.

questions.q: List, in order, the five steps a particle accelerator uses to discover and study particles (the 'All Scientists Crave Cool Data' chain).
keyPoints: Accelerate — electric fields give charged particles repeated energy kicks, raising their kinetic energy.
Steer — magnetic fields bend the particles onto curved/circular paths (the magnetic field does no work, it only steers).
Collide — the high-energy particles are smashed into a fixed target or head-on into an opposing beam.
Convert — the collision's kinetic energy is converted into the mass of new particles via E = mc^2.
Detect — detectors record the tracks, charges, momenta and energies, letting physicists identify the particles.
questions.explanation: The mark-earning distinction is electric fields accelerate while magnetic fields only steer, plus the energy-to-mass conversion (E = mc^2) and detection step. 'They smash particles and see what comes out' earns almost nothing.

questions.q: Why does a nucleus packed with mutually repelling protons not fly apart, given the role of the strong nuclear force described in the episode?
options: The strong force is weak but long-range, so it reaches across the whole nucleus to overcome repulsion

The strong force is the strongest of the four forces but acts only over an extremely short range (about \(10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}\)); at the tiny separations inside a nucleus its attraction between neighbouring nucleons beats the long-range Coulomb repulsion
The electromagnetic repulsion between protons is cancelled by gravity
Gluons give the protons a neutral charge, so they no longer repel
questions.explanation: The strong force is the strongest force but is a short-range, nearest-neighbour force acting over about \(10^{-15}\,\mathrm{m}\). At nuclear separations its attraction between adjacent nucleons exceeds the long-range Coulomb repulsion between protons, so the nucleus holds together.

questions.q: Compare the role of the strong nuclear force and the weak nuclear force within the nucleus. (4 marks)
questions.modelAnswer: The strong nuclear force binds quarks together inside protons and neutrons and, as a residual effect, binds the protons and neutrons together in the nucleus; whereas the weak nuclear force is responsible for radioactive beta decay, in which it transforms one type of quark into another, changing a neutron into a proton or a proton into a neutron. The strong force is carried by gluons and is the strongest of the four fundamental forces; in contrast, the weak force is carried by the W and Z bosons and is far weaker. In essence, the strong force holds the nucleus together, whereas the weak force transforms particles and drives decay.

criteria.descriptor: States the strong force binds quarks within nucleons and binds nucleons in the nucleus.
States the weak force is responsible for beta decay / transforms one quark type into another.
Identifies the carriers: gluons (strong) versus W and Z bosons (weak), and relative strength.
Leads with the central contrast: strong holds matter together, weak transforms particles.

questions.explanation: Use explicit contrast language ('whereas', 'in contrast'). The single most important mark is the role contrast: strong binds, weak transforms.
